Conduct the cross wavelet transform on a time series or signal

Source: R/analyse_Xwavelet.R, R/zzz_aliases_american.R
analyse_Xwavelet.Rd

Compute the cross wavelet transform using a complex Morlet wavelet based on the "analyze.coherency" function of the WaveletComp package.

Usage

analyse_Xwavelet(
  data_1,
  data_2,
  dj = 1/100,
  lowerPeriod = 2,
  upperPeriod = 1024,
  verbose = FALSE,
  omega_nr = 4,
  wavelet = "morlet",
  wavelet_order = NULL
)

analyze_Xwavelet(
  data_1,
  data_2,
  dj = 1/100,
  lowerPeriod = 2,
  upperPeriod = 1024,
  verbose = FALSE,
  omega_nr = 4,
  wavelet = "morlet",
  wavelet_order = NULL
)

Arguments

data_1

First record: a matrix or data frame with depth/time in column 1 and the proxy value in column 2 (no NA values). Both records are sorted and linearly interpolated to a common, regular grid over their overlapping interval, with the coarser of the two median sampling intervals. Required, no default.

data_2

Second record, in the same format and depth/time unit as data_1 (matrix or data frame: depth/time in column 1, proxy value in column 2). The cross phase is the phase of data_1 minus that of data_2. Required, no default.

dj

Spacing between successive scales in octaves (numeric, > 0), passed to analyse_wavelet: the periods increase by powers of 2 and dj=1/x gives x periods per doubling of the period. Smaller values give a finer period axis but increase the computation time. Default=1/100.

lowerPeriod

Shortest period to analyse, in the same unit as the depth/time column of the records (numeric, > 0; at least twice the common sampling interval). Default=2.

upperPeriod

Longest period to analyse, in the same unit as the depth/time column of the records (numeric, > lowerPeriod). Default=1024.

verbose

Print the sampling interval to which the records were interpolated, passed to analyse_wavelet (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

omega_nr

Number of cycles (central angular frequency omega_0) of the Morlet wavelet, passed to analyse_wavelet (numeric, > 0). Larger values give a better period resolution and a worse depth/time resolution. Default=4.

wavelet

Mother wavelet (character string or function), given as a name (PyWavelets style names with the order appended, such as "db4", "sym8", "cgau3", "gaus2" or "cmor1.5-1", also work) or as a function psi_hat(omega) that returns the Fourier transform of a user defined mother wavelet. Analytic (complex) wavelets, which give phase and amplitude and can be synchrosqueezed: "morlet" (default; aliases "gabor", "amor"), "morlet0" (exactly zero mean Morlet, admissible for a small omega_nr; alias "morlex"), "paul" (alias "cauchy"), "morse" (generalised Morse wavelet of Olhede and Walden, 2002; aliases "gmw", "airy"), "bump", "cmor" (complex Morlet with bandwidth and centre frequency as in Matlab/PyWavelets), "cgau" (analytic Gaussian derivative; "cmhat" is the complex Mexican hat), "shannon" (complex Shannon, box spectrum), "fbsp" (frequency B-spline), "meyer", "loggabor" (alias "lognormal"), "gammatone" (asymmetric in time: sharp onset, slow decay) and "hann" (raised cosine band). Real wavelets, which give a real transform (no phase or envelope): "dog" (derivative of Gaussian; "mexh", "ricker", "marr" and "sombrero" are the Mexican hat, order 2), "morl" (real Morlet), "hhat" (Hermitian hat), "poisson", and the orthogonal wavelets "haar", "db" (Daubechies), "sym" (Symlets) and "battle" (Battle-Lemarie spline wavelets), which are computed in the frequency domain from their filters. The period axis of the orthogonal wavelets is approximate because their spectra are broad and not symmetric. A narrow wavelet (Paul, low-order DOG, Shannon, Haar) resolves position well, a wide one (Morse with a large beta, Morlet with a high omega_nr, bump) resolves period well. Default="morlet".

wavelet_order

Parameter(s) of the wavelet (numeric scalar or vector; NULL uses the defaults listed here): paul: order m (default 4); dog: derivative m (default 2); morse: c(gamma, beta) or beta alone with gamma = 3 (default c(3, 20)); bump: c(mu, sigma) (default c(5, 0.6)); cmor: c(bandwidth, centre frequency) (default c(1.5, 1)); cgau: derivative m (default 4); shannon: c(bandwidth, centre frequency) (default c(2, 1.5)); fbsp: c(m, bandwidth, centre frequency) (default c(2, 2, 1.5)); loggabor: c(centre angular frequency, log-width) (default c(6, 0.25)); meyer and hhat have no parameter; morlet0: omega_0 (default omega_nr); morl: omega_0 (default 5); poisson: order n (default 2); gammatone: c(n, centre angular frequency, bandwidth) (default c(4, 6, 1.5)); hann: c(centre angular frequency, half width) (default c(6, 3)); db: number of vanishing moments 1 to 20 (default 4, "haar" = "db1"); sym: 2 to 20 (default 8); battle: spline order 1, 3, 5 or 7 (default 3). Passed to analyse_wavelet; for the Morlet wavelet use omega_nr. Default=NULL.

Value

A list with class "analyze.Xwavelet" containing Wave: complex wavelet coefficients Power: time frequency power spectrum dt: sampling interval after interpolation Phase: instantaneous phase of the signal dj: number of frequencies Power.avg: average spectral power Period: physical periods corresponding to frequencies nc: number of columns in the input data nr: number of frequency levels axis.1: x axis values (time or depth) axis.2: y axis values (log2 scaled periods) c1: base number of wavelet cycles o: numeric vector of length two defining the minimum and maximum superlet order. If NULL, all frequencies are analysed using order one. x1: interpolated x values first data set y1: interpolated signal values first data set x2: interpolated x values second data set y2: interpolated signal values second data set

References

Moca, V. V., Bârzan, H., Nagy-Dăbâcan, A., & Mureșan, R. C. (2021). Time-frequency super-resolution with superlets. Nature Communications, 12(1), 337. doi:10.1038/s41467-020-20539-9

Author

The "analyse_Xsuperlet" that generates the input for the plotting function is based on the matlab code in Moca et al. (2021) and the the "analyze.coherency" function of the 'WaveletComp' R package

Examples

# \donttest{
#Example 1. A cross superlet of two etp solutions with noise overprint
etp_1 <- astrochron::etp(
 tmin = 0,
 tmax = 500,
 dt = 2,
 eWt = 1.5,
 oWt = 0.75,
 pWt = 1,
 esinw = TRUE,
 standardize = TRUE,
 genplot = FALSE,
 verbose = FALSE
)

etp_2 <- astrochron::etp(
 tmin = 0,
 tmax = 500,
 dt = 2,
 eWt = 1,
 oWt = 0.5,
 pWt = 1.5,
 esinw = TRUE,
 standardize = TRUE,
 genplot = FALSE,
 verbose = FALSE
)

etp_1[, 2] <- etp_1[, 2] + wr_coloured_noise(
 nrow(etp_1),
 sd = sd(etp_1[, 2]) / 1.5,
 mean = mean(etp_1[, 2]),
 phi = 0.9
)
etp_2[, 2] <- etp_2[, 2] + wr_coloured_noise(
 nrow(etp_2),
 sd = sd(etp_2[, 2]) / 1.5,
 mean = mean(etp_2[, 2]),
 phi = 0.9
)

Xetp <- analyse_Xwavelet(
 data_1 = etp_1,
 data_2  = etp_2,
 upperPeriod = 512,
     dj = 1/20,
 lowerPeriod = 4,
 verbose = FALSE,
 omega_nr = 8
)
# }
